notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded implementation of the official 2025 C++ RTI/encoding/HLAfixedArray.h class. IEEE 1516.2 §4.14.10.4 defines HLAfixedArray as a fixed-cardinality sequence whose first element begins at offset zero. For each nonfinal element, Equation (5) chooses the smallest nonnegative padding needed to reach the sole element type's octet boundary; the general constructed-type source also requires padding bytes to be zero. No padding follows the final element, and the encoded size includes inter-element padding. The Requirements Lab exports direct sequence and no-trailing-padding candidates with broad clause-4 metadata although the reconstructed heading is §4.14.10.4; it does not export a separate immutable candidate for Equation (5) or the zero-byte statement. RL-054 records both provenance and candidate-coverage boundaries. The official C++ header expressly assigns raw element-pointer lifetime responsibility to the caller, so Umbra retains those pointers as borrowed, non-owning storage and copies/clone operations use internal memory. That lifetime policy is an implementation safety choice, not a separate standards or conformance result. This does not establish HLAvariableArray or variant-record support, model-specific encoder factories, adapter exposure, interoperability, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, or conformance.
